reason: The newline-delimited JSON-RPC transport and the named SDK message types are kept as two packages of the standard-library-only module src/sdk: the bounded codec sdk/jsonrpc and sdk/protocol, which adds a method table, an integer protocol version and one error table.

The stdio serving plugin becomes the cordis component wire.sdk: explicit session create, resume, close and cancel, history reads, host-scoped notifications, a run result per claimed turn, and approvals and questions answered through the interaction registry.

The TypeScript client library is replaced by a public Go client package for Go programs and the harness itself, and by TypeScript declarations and stubs generated from the protocol schema file for a TypeScript consumer; the result interval and tree scoping it computed are now host facts.

The automation-only ACP v1 agent on stdio is kept as component wire.acp behind the acpwire wrapper, with truthful capabilities, settlement at quiescence and rollback of a failed setup; changed are the stop-reason mapping for failed turns and support for additional directories.

The build-time TypeScript analyser and artifact generator exists to recover erased types; Go derives schemas from its types by reflection when they are registered, and the one remaining emitter is the protocol schema document derived from the method table and held equal by a test.

It exists only because of npm and generated JavaScript: it imports each mounted npm package's generated ./typert export at run time. The Go design generates no artifact and loads no package, so there is nothing to discover or register.

What survives is folded into the codec and the protocol package: the single failure type with domain/reason codes becomes jsonrpc.Error and the shared error table, and the invocation descriptor idea becomes the method table. The Remote decorators, lookup maps and browser event forwarding are not built because no browser application calls host methods.

The runtime registry of generated reflection, schema factories and invocation descriptors is replaced by the schema package, which derives and caches a schema per Go type, and by static method tables; no service holds them because compiled-in types are never unloaded.

The inventory matched a regular expression in the generator that reads @deprecated tags out of doc comments; nothing at this line is deprecated, and the TypeScript generator it belongs to is not built.

ACP session/new accepts additionalDirectories: each becomes a session write root registered through the sandbox policy resolver in the agent's scope, advertised only when that service is mounted, and rolled back with the agent if any directory is invalid.
ACP prompts still accept text, resource links and raster images only, and images only when an attachment store is mounted and the route accepts them; audio and embedded resources are refused.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-SDK-9: the model input vocabulary of the harness is text and raster images, so no other block has a consumer, and advertising image support only when the store and route exist is the truthful-capability rule the design requires, not a defect.

reason: A client-supplied MCP server is mounted through the harness MCP client, so an ACP session gets exactly what that client consumes; this area adds no consumer for MCP resources or prompts.
justification: The limit belongs to the MCP client of area A15, not to the ACP carrier: decision DH-ADR-SDK-9 only mounts the server in the agent's scope. If area A15 gives resources or prompts a consumer, ACP sessions gain it with no change here.

reason: The ACP surface still offers no session/load replay, no delete or fork, and no modes, commands, plans, terminals, client file operations or elicitation.
justification: Kept on purpose by decisions DH-ADR-SDK-9 and DH-ADR-WIRE-7: ACP is an automation transport and presentation belongs to the web UI. A program that needs the transcript reads session/history on the SDK protocol; replay through session/load is recorded as an open question for the owner.

reason: There is no package to resolve a runtime from: the harness is one static binary, every client takes one explicit path or the DSH_BIN variable, and the Python wheel carries the binary inside it.

The protocol has session/cancel to stop a turn or step, session/close to dispose an agent and a $/cancel notification for an in-flight request, so stopping runtime work no longer requires closing the harness; a local timeout still never cancels work by itself.

A prompt's result is no longer a receipt-to-idle interval: the session log records which turn claimed each message, and the host reports that one turn's ending and last assistant message, so other queued work is never included.

A handler in the Go client receives a context that is cancelled when the host withdraws the request, the connection is lost or the client closes; a handler that ignores it keeps running in the caller's process.
justification: No Go mechanism stops a goroutine, so the limit cannot be removed. Decision DH-ADR-SDK-8 bounds its effect: the late answer is never sent, the host has already settled the request as refused, and Close returns after a bounded wait and names the handlers still running.

reason: initialize negotiates an integer protocol version: the client lists the versions it speaks, the host picks the highest common one or fails with sdk/version-unsupported, and only additive changes are allowed inside a version.
The protocol defines session/cancel and session/close, so a client abandons a turn or releases a session without closing the runtime process.
A pending question or approval still lives in one host process: after a restart its request cannot be answered, the interrupted turn is closed and the model may ask again.
justification: Kept on purpose: the design never continues an interrupted turn and never restores a pending interaction after a restart (design section 5, decision DH-ADR-WIRE-4), because failing closed costs one more prompt. Decision DH-ADR-SDK-6 applies that rule to the SDK connection.

reason: session/close disposes one agent and releases its lease while the session stays stored, and session/cancel stops a turn or a step, so agents created for a client no longer stay live until process shutdown.

The host sends session.run.completed for every accepted prompt and command, naming the turn that claimed the message, its reason, its final assistant text and its position in the log; clients no longer define and observe an interval.

Standard output is claimed once by the stdio component, which keeps the real handle private and points the process-wide os.Stdout at standard error; child processes never inherit it, and a test captures stdout with every logger forced on.
The carrier mounts no model adapter at all: a session's route is validated by exact id through the model runtime, and an unknown provider fails create or initialize with no vendor-specific fallback.
Wildcard patterns in npm package exports exist only in the npm package format that the TypeScript generator analyses; Go has no package export map and no generator runs.
Namespace re-exports across host and client faces are a TypeScript module construct between two separately compiled programs; the Go design has one program and no faces.

The Zod emitter and the conditional and mapped types it cannot emit are TypeScript constructs; no emitter exists. The Go counterpart, a Go type that reflection cannot describe, fails a test that derives every registered type instead of failing a build step.
Merging unions of named fields and index signatures into strict schemas is a property of TypeScript's structural type algebra; a Go struct has one fixed field set, so there are no operands to merge.
Generated schema imports across faces concern generated JavaScript modules for two compiled programs; nothing is generated and there is one program.
Discovery through the reachable graph of public TypeScript exports belongs to the generator's analysis; in Go a type takes part by being registered explicitly, so there is no discovery step to limit.
Importing only the host face's generated artifact is a limit of a two-program client and host build; the UI is rendered by the host, so there is no client face to discover.
Explicit package entries for nested plugins exist because loader fibers carry no resolvable npm package specifier; Go components are compiled in and nothing is located by package name.
A cached verdict about whether an npm package exports ./typert can only go stale when packages change in a running process; the Go host never loads code at run time.

There is no asynchronous registration to wait for: the method table is a Go value complete at program start, handlers are checked against it by a test, and the carrier answers initialize only when boot reports the tree ready.

A row of the method table carries the name, direction, kind, parameter and result types, capability, first version and description, and schemas come from the Go types by reflection, so full metadata needs no build pipeline.

The restrictions concern TypeScript decorators and signatures (overloads, destructuring, defaults, rest parameters); a Go handler has one form, a context and one parameter struct in, one result and an error out.
Merging host and client type graphs presupposes two faces and TypeScript references to resolve; one Go program has one set of types.
Schema keys that omit the face can only collide when two faces register into one context; there are no faces and schemas are keyed by Go type.
The schema package derives a JSON Schema once per Go type and caches the immutable result for the life of the process, and the protocol document is computed once, so no consumer has to own caching.
The config becomes the Go struct acpserver.Config with the same three fields: an optional default provider and model, and sessionListPageSize with default 100 and bounds 1 to 1000, decoded strictly.

The one upstream field, maxTokensAsSuccess, is not carried because the host reports the finish reason and the client decides what counts as success. The Go structs sdkserver.Config and stdio.Config hold the limits the transport lacked: in-flight requests, history page size, frame size, queue size, write stall and exit deadline.
Its single field lists npm packages whose generated ./typert export should be imported; it exists only because of npm packages and generated JavaScript, and no Go component reads such a list.

ctx.typert has no Go service key. Its jobs are done by the schema package function schema.Of (schemas by reflection, cached per type), by the static method table protocol.Methods (invocation descriptors) and by each registry's own catalog output.

title: The SDK transport has no defences: malformed lines are dropped silently, every handler failure crosses as free text under one code, and frames and the outbound queue are unbounded

reason: The Go codec answers a malformed line with a parse error and a stderr line, bounds the frame size and the outbound queue, ends a connection whose pipe accepts nothing for the stall deadline, and reports failures by a domain/reason code with no internal text.

title: Any SDK method that names an unknown session id creates a session, including a working-directory read, so a mistyped id silently becomes a new session

reason: Only session/create creates a session; every other method that names a session the connection has not created or resumed fails with sdk/session-not-owned or session/not-found and creates nothing.

The principle is kept and the mechanism replaced: one canonical model that every output is derived from, and an emitter that fails instead of degrading a type, are provided by the reflected schema of each Go type; the compiler-based extraction, the two faces and the type graph have no Go counterpart.

One failure type with a domain/reason code and typed details, declared once by the package that owns the failure and discriminated by code, is kept as jsonrpc.Error and the single error table of every stdio surface; unclassified failures fold to rpc/internal. The browser-only parts (fixed host facts on ctx.remote, cross-realm markers) are not carried.

The goal is adopted: one static description per method from which schemas, typed clients and reference documentation are derived offline. The Go form is the method table of the SDK protocol and the schema file derived from it; the generated ESM artifacts and the two input-strictness codecs are replaced by strict decoding on the host and tolerant decoding in clients.

Kept: a client advertises a question handler in the handshake, the carrier routes the question tool to it only for agents the connection owns, validates that every question id is answered exactly once, treats a dismissal as never an approval and ignores late answers. Changed: the host withdraws a question with the codec's $/cancel instead of a separate request id and notification.

ACP stays an automation transport that carries session controls, one prompt at a time, committed semantic updates, cancellation and one-shot permission requests, and no presentation. Changed in Go: a turn that ended in error fails the prompt instead of reporting end_turn, and additional directories are supported as session write roots.

title: One codec and one error table for every line-delimited JSON-RPC pipe
The protocol is declared once: Go message types and a method table
An integer protocol version, negotiated once, with additive change inside a version
Sessions are created, resumed and closed explicitly, and belong to the connection
A run is the turn that claimed the input, and the host reports it
Approvals, questions and client tools are host requests; withdrawal is $/cancel; every doubt is a refusal
One writer, a log-tailing forwarder per session, and a stall deadline instead of an overflow kill
A third module, src/sdk, holds the codec, the protocol types and the Go client; the three modules are tagged together
ACP stays automation-only, with a stated mapping to harness sessions and turns
Typert is not built; what is left of its job is the schema package and the method table
Standard output belongs to exactly one stdio carrier, by construction
A bounded JSON-RPC codec with one error table
The SDK protocol as Go types, a method table and a derived schema file
One owner of stdin and stdout, with a bounded exit
An SDK program can create, resume, prompt, cancel, close and read sessions
The host reports run results and scoped, ordered notifications
A client answers approvals and questions over the same connection
A client can offer its own functions to the model as tools
A Go program drives the harness through a public client package
An ACP client drives the harness, and the harness can drive an ACP agent
A protocol reference page
A generated TypeScript client
Framing: the three message kinds round-trip and malformed input gives the tabled error
Limits: frame size, in-flight requests and the method allow-list are enforced
Cancellation crosses the wire in both directions and close fails pending calls once
Frames keep enqueue order, the barrier holds and a stalled writer ends the connection
The derived protocol document equals the checked-in schema file
Method table and handlers match in both directions; every error reason is a declared constant
Version negotiation, the initialize gate and strict request decoding
Explicit session lifecycle: nothing is created implicitly and leases are released on close
The watermark rule and gap-free ordered events per session
A run result names exactly the turn that claimed the message
Command and goal completion; notifications are scoped and carry root and parent
History paging returns every event once; a resent message id produces no second turn
Approvals over the wire settle as refused on every abnormal path
Question answers are validated, dismissal is not approval, withdrawal cancels
A slow client bounds host memory and loses no durable event
The Go client against a fake host: results, handlers, cancellation and the close ladder
The sdk module imports only the standard library, the three modules are required and tagged at one version, and the client fails before start without a home or binary
Every row of the ACP mapping, including quiescent settlement and the stop-reason table
ACP capabilities are truthful and a failed session setup leaves nothing behind
ACP close, disconnect and unload run one teardown, once, child-first
Every stdout line of the sdk and acp profiles is a protocol frame; a second claim fails
Each way a connection ends makes one stop request to boot with its status, and boot's shutdown bound forces the exit
A client-declared tool passes the whole pipeline and settles as outcome unknown on a lost pipe
The reference page equals what the schema file generates
The TypeScript declarations and stubs equal what the schema file generates
The user's time zone given at initialize or at session create reaches the clock context, an unknown zone is refused, and no zone means unavailable
A Go program drives the built binary against a real model API
A client that dies or stops reading never leaves a host behind
An ACP client uses a real MCP server and an extra directory, then resumes
